description: Makes links to the app's web open the app itself: writes .well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS Universal Links) and .well-known/assetlinks.json (Android App Links) into the web project's public folder (public/, Flutter's web/), from what Ploa knows: the bundle ID and the Apple team of the App Store connection, the package name and the SHA-256 of the upload key Ploa keeps. Google Play re-signs every install with its own app signing key, so pass that key's SHA-256 too (androidFingerprints): the person reads it in Play Console › Test and release › App integrity › App signing; links don't open the app from Play installs without it. paths: the paths the app opens (default every path, "*"; "/invite/*" opens only those). The files go live with the next ploa_web_build. The answer says what the app's own config needs (Expo: ios.associatedDomains and android.intentFilters with autoVerify); Ploa turns on Associated Domains at Apple when the build's entitlements ask for it. Only on the MCP server on this computer.

androidFingerprints.description: SHA-256 fingerprints of Google Play's app signing key (Play Console › App integrity › App signing), in any form (AB:CD:… or plain hex).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

folder.description: Absolute path of the folder whose files the web build copies as they are, when it isn't public/ (or Flutter's web/).

paths.description: The paths the app opens, like "/invite/*". Default: every path ("*").

site.description: The site's address (the part before .ploa.app) or ID. Needed when the workspace has more than one site.

teamId.description: The Apple team ID, when the App Store connection has no signing certificate yet (Apple Developer › Membership details).

name: ploa_app_links
title: Make links open the app
